identification.summary: Microsoft describes Charcoal Typhoon (formerly CHROMIUM) as a Chinese state-affiliated threat actor with a broad operational scope, targeting government, higher education, communications infrastructure, oil and gas, and information technology, mainly in Taiwan, Thailand, Mongolia, Malaysia, France and Nepal, and also institutions and individuals worldwide who oppose China's policies [S1]. In February 2024 Microsoft and OpenAI reported that the group had used large language models for research, scripting, translation and phishing content, and disabled its accounts [S1][S2]. In March 2025 the FBI said that activity of the PRC contractor i-Soon (Anxun Information Technology) is tracked by industry as Aquatic Panda, BRONZE UNIVERSITY, Charcoal Typhoon, Earth Lusca and RedHotel [S3][S4].
identification.firstObserved: Trend Micro (as summarized in a Singapore IMDA advisory): Earth Lusca active since at least April 2019 [S12]. Trend Micro had been tracking Earth Lusca since mid-2021 when it published its 2022 brief [S11]. The FBI places i-Soon intrusions from about 2016 to 2023 [S3][S4]. Microsoft does not give a first-observed date in the sources gathered [S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Charcoal Typhoon (formerly CHROMIUM). Microsoft lists Aquatic Panda, ControlX, RedHotel and BRONZE UNIVERSITY as other researchers' names [S1]. The FBI's 2025 statement adds Earth Lusca to the i-Soon cluster [S3][S4]. ESET tracks FishMonger, which it says is operated by I-SOON and also tracked as Earth Lusca, TAG-22, Aquatic Panda and Red Dev 10 [S5]. Recorded Future's TAG-22 (2021) and RedHotel (2023) reports describe overlapping activity [S6][S7]. MITRE tracks Aquatic Panda as G0143 and Earth Lusca as a separate group, G1006 [S13]. The imported summary in this record is Earth Lusca text, not Microsoft's description of Charcoal Typhoon.

attribution.sponsor: People's Republic of China. Microsoft calls Charcoal Typhoon Chinese state-affiliated [S1]. US prosecutors (as reported in press coverage) allege that i-Soon, whose activity the FBI ties to Charcoal Typhoon, hacked at the direction of and in close coordination with the Ministry of State Security (MSS) and the Ministry of Public Security (MPS), and tried to sell stolen data to at least 43 MSS/MPS bureaus in at least 31 provinces and municipalities [S3][S4]. Recorded Future assessed that RedHotel's targeting, tooling and methods closely resemble other MSS-affiliated private contractor groups, and linked its infrastructure administration to Chengdu [S7].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft states the attribution as a Chinese state-affiliated actor [S1]. ESET assesses with high confidence that FishMonger conducted Operation FishMedley and says it independently confirmed FishMonger is operated by I-SOON [S5]. Trend Micro calls the Earth Lusca and i-Soon overlap significant but says its research was still ongoing [S10]. The US government brought formal criminal charges against i-Soon employees and MPS officers in March 2025 [S3][S4]; the FBI's mapping of vendor names to i-Soon is the government link to the Charcoal Typhoon name [S3][S4].
attribution.basis: Microsoft and OpenAI account telemetry [S1][S2]; DOJ indictment and FBI statements (via press coverage) [S3][S4]; Trend Micro overlaps in victims, tooling (ShadowPad, Winnti) and Chengdu source IPs with the leaked i-Soon data [S10]; ESET intrusion analysis [S5]; Recorded Future infrastructure analysis [S6][S7].

objectives: Espionage that supports PRC government priorities: government, foreign-affairs, telecommunications and academic intelligence across Asia and globally, plus monitoring of people and institutions who oppose China's policies [S1][S9]. Recorded Future assessed that some targeting, such as Taiwan's ITRI and COVID-19 research, was likely industrial and economic espionage [S7]. Trend Micro reports possible financial motivation from attacks on gambling and cryptocurrency firms [S11]. Under the contractor model described by prosecutors, i-Soon both received tasking from officials and chose its own targets to sell stolen data to MSS/MPS bureaus [S3][S4].

sectors: Government, including foreign ministries and foreign-affairs departments [S1][S3][S9]
Research and development, aerospace and think tanks [S5][S6][S7][S10]
NGOs, religious organizations and pro-democracy/human-rights groups [S3][S5][S11]
regions: Taiwan, Thailand, Mongolia, Malaysia, France, Nepal (Microsoft) [S1]
Seventeen countries across Asia, Europe and North America, including the Philippines, Hong Kong, India, Vietnam, Pakistan and the US (RedHotel, 2021-2023) [S7]
Southeast Asia, Central Asia and the Balkans (Earth Lusca, H1 2023) [S9]
Taiwan, Hungary, Turkey, Thailand, the US and France (FishMedley, 2022) [S5]
United States: DIA, Commerce Department, a US religious organization and news outlets; foreign ministries of India, Indonesia, South Korea and Taiwan (i-Soon indictment) [S3][S4]
targeting.notes: Regions and sectors come from several overlapping vendor clusters (Microsoft Charcoal Typhoon, Recorded Future TAG-22/RedHotel, Trend Micro Earth Lusca, ESET FishMonger) and from the i-Soon indictment. They are combined here on the basis of the FBI and ESET alias mappings [S3][S5], not because Microsoft confirmed each victim set.

capabilities.summary: Initial access through exploitation of internet-facing servers: Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) on VMware Horizon at an academic institution [S8], compromised GlassFish servers [S6], and 2019-2022 n-day flaws on public-facing servers [S9]; also spear-phishing, watering holes and geopolitical lure documents [S10][S11]. Post-exploitation includes Cobalt Strike, attempts to disable EDR, LSASS credential dumping and WinRAR staging for exfiltration [S8][S9]. Lateral movement uses Impacket with privileged access [S5]. Long-term access relies on shared PRC malware families (ShadowPad, Winnti, Spyder, SodaMaster) [S5][S6][S12] and the custom Linux backdoor SprySOCKS, derived from Trochilus [S9]. VPS reverse proxies hide C2 [S7]. Microsoft and OpenAI observed the group using LLMs to research companies, platforms, vulnerabilities and security tools, generate and debug scripts, translate, and draft phishing content; OpenAI judged this a limited, incremental uplift [S1][S2].

campaigns.summary: Recorded Future reported to clients on activity by a user of the shared Winnti and ShadowPad backdoors against a Hong Kong university and airport; it was later folded into TAG-22.

campaigns.summary: Telecom, academic, R&D and government organizations were compromised via GlassFish servers and Cobalt Strike, followed by Winnti, ShadowPad and Spyder.

campaigns.name: Log4Shell exploitation of an academic institution (Aquatic Panda)
campaigns.summary: CrowdStrike OverWatch saw a modified Log4j exploit used against VMware Horizon, followed by reconnaissance, attempts to disable EDR and LSASS dumping; the victim's patching stopped further activity.

campaigns.name: Earth Lusca worldwide operations
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro described spear-phishing and watering-hole campaigns against government, education, media, pro-democracy, gambling and cryptocurrency targets.

campaigns.name: Operation FishMedley
campaigns.summary: ESET documented FishMonger compromising seven organizations (governments, NGOs, think tanks) in Asia, Europe and the US with ShadowPad, SodaMaster and Spyder; published March 2025.

campaigns.name: RedHotel multi-country espionage
campaigns.summary: Recorded Future identified victims in 17 countries across academia, aerospace, government, media, telecom and research, with infrastructure administration linked to Chengdu.

campaigns.name: Earth Lusca SprySOCKS campaign
campaigns.summary: Exploitation of public-facing servers targeted foreign-affairs, technology and telecom government bodies in Southeast Asia, Central Asia and the Balkans, with the new Linux backdoor SprySOCKS.

campaigns.name: Taiwan election-period geopolitical lure
campaigns.summary: Earth Lusca used a likely stolen Taiwanese geopolitical document, created two days before Taiwan's election, to target a Taiwan-based think tank. The campaign ran about December 2023 to January 2024.

campaigns.name: LLM misuse disrupted by Microsoft and OpenAI
campaigns.summary: Charcoal Typhoon accounts used for research, scripting, translation and phishing content were terminated.

campaigns.name: US charges against i-Soon employees and MPS officers
campaigns.summary: DOJ charged i-Soon personnel and two MPS officers. The FBI tied i-Soon to Aquatic Panda, BRONZE UNIVERSITY, Charcoal Typhoon, Earth Lusca and RedHotel; victims included the DIA, Commerce, and several foreign ministries.

diamond.adversary: PRC contractor i-Soon (Anxun Information Technology) personnel working with MSS and MPS, per US charges [S3][S4]; Chinese state-affiliated actor per Microsoft [S1]; infrastructure administration linked to Chengdu [S7][S10].
diamond.capability: N-day exploitation of internet-facing servers (Log4Shell, GlassFish, others) [S6][S8][S9]; spear-phishing and watering holes [S11]; Cobalt Strike, ShadowPad, Winnti, Spyder, SodaMaster, SprySOCKS [S5][S6][S9]; Impacket and LSASS credential theft [S5][S8]; LLM-assisted research and scripting [S1].
diamond.infrastructure: Actor-controlled C2 [S6]; VPS reverse proxies for C2 [S7]; delivery servers hosting encrypted payloads [S9].
diamond.victim: Governments and foreign ministries, universities, telecoms, IT, oil and gas, think tanks, NGOs, religious and pro-democracy groups, media, and gambling/crypto firms across Asia, Europe and North America [S1][S3][S5][S7][S9][S11].
diamond.socioPolitical: Intelligence collection for PRC state customers through a hacker-for-hire market, where stolen data is sold to MSS/MPS bureaus [S3][S4]; monitoring of opponents of PRC policy [S1]; interest in Taiwan politics around elections [S10].
diamond.technology: Exposed and unpatched internet-facing services (VMware Horizon, GlassFish, other public-facing servers), Windows and Linux server estates, and endpoint security that the actor attempts to disable [S6][S8][S9].

gaps: Primary DOJ indictment, DOJ press release and FBI wanted notice could not be opened (government sites blocked); indictment details come from press coverage [S3][S4].

Microsoft's threat-actor naming table (learn.microsoft.com) could not be fetched to confirm the current Microsoft alias list; Microsoft's 2024 blog does not list Earth Lusca, TAG-22 or FishMonger as Charcoal Typhoon names [S1].

Cluster boundaries: MITRE keeps Aquatic Panda (G0143) and Earth Lusca (G1006) as separate groups, and the shared tooling (ShadowPad, Winnti) is used by multiple PRC actors [S6][S13]. Treat the merged victim and TTP picture as cluster-level, not confirmed single-actor.

ESET WeLiveSecurity FishMedley report, Trend Micro primary reports, Recorded Future RedHotel PDF and the CrowdStrike Log4Shell blog were not opened directly; details come from search-result summaries, translated copies or press coverage.
CrowdStrike's Aquatic Panda adversary profile (stated start date, dual intelligence and industrial-espionage mission) could not be read in full or dated.
Post-indictment activity (2025-2026) attributed to Charcoal Typhoon by Microsoft was not found in the sources gathered.
No public reporting gathered on any targeting of US military or Air Force networks beyond the DIA victim named in the indictment coverage [S3].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (OE): Key cyber terrain is internet-facing servers (VMware Horizon/Log4j, GlassFish, other n-day-exposed services) and the Linux and Windows hosts behind them in government, academic, telecom and defense-intelligence networks [S3][S6][S8][S9]. STEP 2 (effects): The actor relies on known, often older n-days, so patch latency on edge services defines the exposure window. Shared PRC malware complicates attribution [S6][S9]. STEP 3 (adversary template): edge exploitation, spear-phishing or a watering hole leads to Cobalt Strike, then EDR tampering, LSASS dumping and Impacket lateral movement, then ShadowPad, Winnti, Spyder or SprySOCKS for persistence and WinRAR-staged exfiltration through VPS reverse proxies [S5][S7][S8][S9]. STEP 4: MLCOA is persistent espionage against government, foreign-affairs, telecom and academic partners in the Indo-Pacific, with stolen data sold to MSS/MPS customers [S3][S7][S9]. MDCOA is long-dwell compromise of US defense-intelligence or partner-nation foreign-ministry networks around political events such as Taiwan elections [S3][S10]. Candidate indicators: Tomcat or Horizon processes spawning shells or wget/curl; attempts to stop EDR services; LSASS access followed by WinRAR archives; a libmonitor.so.2 loader on Linux; outbound beacons to VPS infrastructure [S8][S9].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: track vendor reporting under all mapped names (Charcoal Typhoon, Aquatic Panda, Earth Lusca, RedHotel, FishMonger, TAG-22) because public reporting is split across vendors [S1][S3][S5]. Authorities: the actor is a contractor indicted under US law and working for MSS/MPS [S3][S4]; defensive and law-enforcement equities (FBI) are active, so coordinate before any response actions beyond DoD networks. Mission assurance: prioritize patching and monitoring of edge services and Linux servers, and protect EDR from tampering, since the sourced intrusions began at exposed services and tried to disable EDR [S8][S9]. Coordination: partner-nation foreign ministries and telecoms in Southeast Asia, Taiwan, Nepal and Mongolia are repeat victims [S1][S3][S6][S9]; share indicators through combatant command and partner CERT channels.

provenance.importedSummary: Earth Lusca is a threat actor from China that targets organizations of interest to the Chinese government, including academic institutions, telecommunication companies, religious organizations, and other civil society groups. Earth Lusca's tools closely resemble those used by Winnti Umbrella, but the group appears to operate separately from Winnti. Earth Lusca has also been observed targeting cryptocurrency payment platforms and cryptocurrency exchanges in what are likely financially motivated attacks.
